title.narrative: SMHI:2023-2025: WACCA-Ethiopia: Water and Climate change for Africa
SMHI:2023-2025: WACCA-Ethiopia: Water and Climate change for Africa

description.narrative:
Objectitve: The WACCA-Ethiopia project aims to address specific capacity gaps in the weather, water and disaster risk reduction (DRR) sectors in Ethiopia. It focuses on developing human technical capacity and the acquisition of necessary skills for weather and water information services, including forecast and early warning systems, as well as improved disaster risk communication and action. The project will improve the production and mode of delivery of key climate adaptation tools and skills including data management and information services from the relevant authorities to key stakeholders and sectors across the country. The overarching goal is to contribute towards long-term national readiness against climate extremes, developing a strong and resilient infrastructure for providing credible and actionable weather, water and disaster risk information for the people of Ethiopia. Climate adaptation will need strong institutions with the ability to deliver actionable information for decision and policy makers at all levels to enhance the quality of life and ensuring sustainable livelihoods for the vulnerable population in Ethiopia.
Impact statement: WACCA-Ethiopia will contribute to improved climate adaptation action by enhancing the readiness toward natural disasters which are projected to increase in frequency with climate change by strengthening the institutional capacity of the national meteorological and hydrological services in Ethiopia.
The project will approach this by building the capacity and skills of personnel at key Ethiopian institutions. The project will contribute to strengthen early warning systems for floods, droughts and other weather- and water-related disasters, allowing for targeted and timely action. This also involves installation and upgrading of relevant meteorological and hydrological systems and data collection infrastructure based on delivered equipment in Phase 1.
The development and effectiveness of the early-warning communication and action will be piloted in selected areas before introducing refined SOPs for early warning systems at a national level. This will be done through continuation of technical training, capacity building and implementation of innovative information and communication technology launched under Phase 1. Adjustments have been made to target and streamline the project to more effectively respond to disaster preparedness, readiness, response and recovery needs.
The focus of WACCA-Ethiopia will be on the promotion of better access to and use of weather and water information and services for decision-making at the community level. The project seeks to improve access to reliable and timely climate information by increasing the capacity of regional and local government officers in the use of climate information. It also aims at increasing local adaptive capacity by ensuring that stakeholders are adequately informed and equipped to understand, use and share climate information with their communities.
The main target groups that will receive capacity building though this programme includes basin administration offices, regional meteorological service centres, hydrological cluster offices, regional and zonal level actors under MoWE, EMI, EDRMC. This includes staff working with forecast and early warning in meteorology and hydrology, data management at key institutions, communication, leadership, and gender mainstreaming who are key users and distributors of the mandated services.
Users of the generated information in the WACCA-Ethiopia Phase 2 project are: 1) institutional and policy makers, 2) general public, 3) actors for disaster risk reduction and prevention. The general public will benefit from using the improved national services, either directly or through institutional users.

Projektet syftar till att åtgärda specifika kapacitetsluckor i väder, vatten och sektorer för att minska risken för katastrofer i Etiopien. Den fokuserar på att utveckla människan teknisk kapacitet och förvärv av erforderlig kompetens för informationstjänster för väder och vatten.

The project aims to address specific capacity gaps in the weather, water and disaster risk reduction sectors in Ethiopia. It focuses on developing human technical capacity and the acquisition of requisite skills for information services for weather and water.

One major result registered in the reporting period is on issues of data sharing and the use of the Hydrological Predictions for the Environment (HYPE) model for managing riverine floods. This was the focus of the second Steering Committee meeting for WACCA-E Phase 2 (held on May 15, 2024). In this meeting, an agreement was reached between MOWE and EMI, to install HYPE at both institutions to support work on riverine flooding (it won't support flash floods as yet). HYPE has the option to support flash floods in the future but this will require more work on the model. It will also require a Ministerial discussion with MOWE and EMI regarding the mandate of flash floods, which all four (SMHI, MOWE, EMI and EDRMC) agreed can be postponed until a later stage.
The following are the results registered at the five work-packages level in the period 2023-06-16 to 2024-06-15.
Work Package 1: Meteorological Information Services
- Training on "DokuWiki" to enable digitalisation of standard operating procedures (SOPs)
- Training in computer programming in Python for meteorological forecasting and analysis
- Research: identified themes (NWP, malaria) & universities (AAU, Arba Minch)
- Dialoge on data sharing conducted.
Work Package 2: Hydrological Information Services
- Training in hydrological modelling theory & practice at SMHI
- More profound AAIT involvement agreed (modelling, field, research)
- Refinement on Ethiopia-HYPE model, partly through remote work
- Dialogue on data sharing
- Dialogues with WMO and FMI.
Work Package 3: Disaster Risk Communication and Action
- Build relationship with EDRMC
- Mapping status & gaps of DRR in Ethiopia including hydromet products & providers, as well as communication & action process
- Work jointly on inter-agency SOP for weather and water hazards
- Draft list of hot-spot areas.
Work Package 4: Data management & ICT
- Installation of all four servers at EMI & MoWE
- New server licences
- Draft of technical workflow for data sharing.
Work Package 5: Sustainable institutions & cooperation
- Progress had been made in terms of understanding and mapping (1) institutions and policies, (2) groups dynamics, leadership coaching management and planning, (3) HR-related, gender and transparency aspects.
- Capacity development for 1) senior- and mid-level management and 2) mid-, and expert-level work process.
- The English version of the SOP for institutional gender mainstreaming has been translated to Amharic during 2023.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
